basic.title: Opening, Wheel, And The First Turn
basic.description: Start at the first real decision: push the shared wheel, read its result, then complete one hand action.

steps.welcome: Seven Hatreds has three victory paths: control 16 regions at New Year, capture an opponent's capital, or reach 3 prestige first.
steps.wheelFirst: The starting setup gives Ming 3 hand cards, and Ming's hand limit is 15. The turn begins by checking whether the hand is over the limit; 3 is not over 15, so this check passes automatically and no card is discarded. The rules then move to the shared wheel.
steps.wheelMove: The wheel has three rule choices: move 1 with no opponent draw; name one opponent to draw 2 cards and move 2; or make every opponent draw 2 cards and move 3. The green destinations only show clickable choices; none is selected yet. Click one destination to execute that exact rule choice.
steps.wheelResult: You just chose the free move of 1, advancing the shared wheel from Military Farm to Recruit / Train. The wheel action has resolved; read the two new regular troops appearing on the map as the result. Once the board change is clear, continue to the hand action.
steps.wheelBranchFinish: The wheel action is complete. Each turn contains one hand action and one wheel action, in either order; this run now takes Ming's hand action, so the next rule is Grant Pardon.
steps.pickAction: It is now the hand-action window. Ming's Grant Pardon rule is: discard 3 hand cards, name one opponent, and have the named player choose one troop adjacent to a Ming-controlled region to move into that adjacent Ming-controlled region and become a Ming troop. Click Grant Pardon to begin paying its cost.
steps.payCards: Grant Pardon is selected, but the map has not changed because its rule requires payment first. Select 3 hand cards and confirm; this step only pays the cost. The map choice appears after the payment is complete.
steps.chooseGrantPardonTarget: The cost is paid. Now apply the troop choice required by the rule: in this run, 1 Later Jin troop moves from Jinzhou into the adjacent Ming-controlled Shanhaiguan and becomes a Ming troop. Click Shanhaiguan to submit that real map choice.
steps.actionResult: Grant Pardon is complete: Jinzhou has 1 fewer Later Jin troop, and Shanhaiguan has 1 more Ming troop. This action changes troop position and faction; it does not directly change Shanhaiguan's control marker to Ming. Control still follows the Shanhaiguan and Jizhen occupation rules.
steps.finish: This first-turn segment now follows the rules: Ming starts with 3 cards, below the 15-card limit, so no discard occurs; the shared wheel resolves Recruit / Train; then the hand action pays 3 cards and resolves Grant Pardon.

attackAndBattle.title: Attack And Field Battle
attackAndBattle.description: Raid starts from a hand action, then flows into field battle, tactics, damage assignment, and retreat handling.

steps.overview: This chapter starts from Ming's normal action window. First take the hand action Raid, pay 1 card, and then read how it creates a field battle.
steps.chooseAction: It is now the hand-action window. Ming's Raid rule is to discard 1 hand card and make an attack action; it cannot use wheel attack dispatch. Click Raid to begin paying the cost.
steps.payRaid: Raid costs 1 hand card. Discard it and confirm; only then does the attack happen. In this run Ming moves from Keshiketeng into adjacent Chahar, so a field battle begins immediately.
steps.borderWidth: Raid has now brought the battle to Chahar. The side panel shows the battle width from Keshiketeng to Chahar: plains can deploy 3 troops, and that width decides how many troops actually fight.
steps.battleOpen: When one player's troops enter a region occupied by another player's troops, a battle begins. Both sides reveal all troops first, then the tactic phase allows one tactic card or no tactic card; tactics are used only in this battle phase.
steps.tacticWindow: Look at the hand area, click Cavalry Charge to select it, then click Play Tactic Card to confirm. The selected card lifts up; click it again to cancel if you picked the wrong card.
steps.battleDamage: The tactic card is now in the battle. Click Rear Guard in the right battle panel to finish this battle resolution; the system rolls artillery, cavalry, then infantry, and each 3 points deals 1 damage.
steps.battleResult: After the field battle resolves, the right post-battle panel keeps the surviving troops and the next handling entry. Read the surviving count there before choosing retreat or another post-battle action.
steps.retreatAndDefeat: In post-battle handling, the losing side chooses rear guard or rout. After it closes, the player strip shows the new defeat marker.
steps.postBattleChoice: The defeat marker is now on the player strip. Use the right post-battle panel to choose the formal closing action; only then will the map show the final troop position and control changes.
steps.finish: Return to the map for the result: troop positions have changed, the right post-battle panel has closed, and the next action window is ready.

siege.title: Siege And Occupation
siege.description: Siege covers defender city withdrawal, city battle resolution, and the post-victory choice between siege and occupation.

steps.overview: This chapter starts with Ming attacking Shanhaiguan. City battle is not just another field battle: defenders can fall back into the city, and the attacker still has to choose siege or occupation after winning.
steps.defendCity: Click Hold City now. The defender moves up to 2 troops and 2 population into Shanhaiguan, while the units left outside keep fighting.
steps.cityBattle: After the defenders enter the city, click Rear Guard in the right battle panel to resolve the city battle. City battle resolves artillery first, then cavalry and infantry; cavalry takes a -1 penalty here.
steps.cityResult: After the city battle, the right post-battle panel keeps the surviving troops and city state. That panel is the formal entry for siege or occupation.
steps.besiegeChoice: Click Besiege first to open the siege options, then click Besiege This Region to confirm. Besieging leaves Ming pressure outside the city, but Shanhaiguan control stays with the defender for the moment.
steps.occupyChoice: After besieging or occupying, look at Shanhaiguan on the map: a siege keeps defender control and leaves the siege state; occupation changes control to Ming and clears the city garrison.
steps.finish: The siege chain closes on the map: the city battle changes surviving troops, then siege or occupation decides Shanhaiguan control and city state.

retreatAndRout.title: Retreat And Rout
retreatAndRout.description: The field-battle loser chooses between rear guard and rout.

steps.overview: This section continues from a lost field battle. The defeated side does not simply disappear; it chooses rear guard or rout as the price of retreat.
steps.chooseRout: Click Rout now. This closes the retreat with heavier losses.
steps.routResult: After routing, the player strip gains 1 defeat marker, and the source region no longer keeps the routed force.
steps.finish: Read the difference in two places: the map shows survivors, while the player strip shows defeat markers.

cavalryPlunder.title: Cavalry Plunder
cavalryPlunder.description: Cavalry can switch to plunder: take artillery/cavalry counterfire first, then plunder population with surviving cavalry and retreat.

steps.overview: Cavalry in field battle does not always have to make a normal attack. When the conditions are right, it can declare plunder.
steps.choosePlunder: Click "Cavalry plunder". This sample plunders the defender deck, then removes population, draws cards, and retreats the cavalry.
steps.plunderResult: After plunder resolves, look at the map first: the target population is lower and the plundering cavalry has returned to its retreat position. The player strip and card areas carry the resource changes.
steps.finish: Cavalry plunder happens during the battle: it takes artillery and cavalry counterfire first, then removes population, draws cards, and retreats based on surviving cavalry.

cavalryEvasion.title: Cavalry Evasion
cavalryEvasion.description: Defending cavalry can leave a field battle for an adjacent friendly region without being treated as routed.

steps.overview: Cavalry can also evade in field battle. Once the defenders leave, the original battle still resolves whether the attacker breaks through.
steps.chooseEvasion: Click the highlighted retreat destination to move the defending cavalry into an adjacent friendly region.
steps.evasionResult: After evasion resolves, look at the map: the defending cavalry has left the original battle and entered the highlighted retreat region; the original battle continues.
steps.finish: Cavalry evasion happens before the battle continues. It changes troop positions on the map first, then the remaining battle resolves without a defeat-retreat penalty.

neutralInvasion.title: Neutral Invasion
neutralInvasion.description: When you attack an unoccupied neutral region with population, neutral defenders are generated for the battle.

steps.overview: A neutral region is not empty when it has population. If an attack enters a neutral region with no player troops, the rule creates level-2 neutral troops from the remaining population (cavalry when the region has horses, otherwise infantry, up to 3) before the battle is resolved.
steps.resolveNeutral: This run attacks Tumed. Click the battle-resolution control so the rule creates neutral defenders from Tumed's population; the region's control changes only after the battle result.
steps.neutralResult: Look back at Tumed on the map: neutral defenders now occupy the region, and because the attacker did not break through, the control marker stays neutral.
steps.finish: Neutral invasion is a battle-resolution rule, not just a map note. Control changes only if the attack actually breaks through.

waterDispatch.title: Water Dispatch
waterDispatch.description: Ming can dispatch through anchor-region sea routes; cavalry dispatch can reach farther, but each sea route still commits at most 2 troops.

steps.overview: Water movement is a formal movement rule. Ming may use sea routes without another card; between two anchor regions, one action moves at most 2 troops, and troops that use water cannot switch to land movement during that action. This run moves from Pidao into Dongjiang.
steps.chooseWaterTarget: Under the water-route rule, click Dongjiang as the map destination. The interface shows the route cost and the limit of 2 troops; the route must continue by water and cannot switch back to land during this action.
steps.waterBoundary: Once the troops enter battle by sea route, this coast boundary has battle width 2, so at most 2 troops can fight on this line. That limit comes from the boundary rule, not from a tutorial-only lock.
steps.finish: After water movement, the normal battle rules still apply: reveal troops, handle tactics, resolve attack order, damage, and victory. Water changes the route and battle width; it does not replace battle resolution.

wheelSharedCost.title: Wheel Branches And Development Actions
wheelSharedCost.description: Longer shared-wheel movement refills opponents and lands the turn in attack, dispatch, diplomacy, or hiring systems.

steps.overview: The shared-wheel push is never free. The farther you move, the more cards your opponents recover, and the more it changes this turn's landing gate.
steps.chooseMove: Pick the shared-wheel move "All opponents draw 2, move 3." This is still the wheel push, not the fight itself.
steps.drawResult: After the wheel moves 3 spaces, look at the player strip: both the Mongols and Later Jin gain 2 hand cards.
steps.dispatchReady: Both opponents have drawn 2 cards and the wheel has moved 3 spaces, so this turn lands on Attack / Dispatch. Under that rule, discard 1 card, move up to 6 troops, and trigger battle only when entering an enemy or non-friendly region.
steps.finish: The shared wheel does more than move a few spaces. It decides which wheel-result action this turn will enter, and who gets cards back because of that push.

wheelReclaim.title: Wheel Reclaim
wheelReclaim.description: Wheel Reclaim directly adds population to a controlled region.

steps.overview: Reclaim is not an off-turn bonus. It is a formal wheel result.
steps.chooseMove: Click the wheel's "Move 1 for free" option to advance the public wheel into Reclaim.
steps.result: Once the wheel lands on Reclaim, look at Xuanfu on the map: population increases by 1. Population later decides taxes, supply, and how much force you can sustain.
steps.finish: Reclaim matters because it thickens the base for later taxes and supply before it gives you more troops.

wheelMilitaryFarm.title: Wheel Military Farm
wheelMilitaryFarm.description: Wheel Military Farm adds both cards and troops.

steps.overview: Military Farm differs from Reclaim because it converts that base directly into current cards and troops.
steps.chooseMove: Click the wheel's "Move 1 for free" option to advance the public wheel from Reclaim into Military Farm.
steps.result: After Wheel Military Farm resolves, look at Xuanfu on the map first: 1 level-2 regular troop appears. The hand-card gain is carried by the player strip.
steps.finish: Military Farm is one of the wheel's clearest snowball actions: your hand grows and your regular force rises with it.

wheelRecruitTrain.title: Wheel Recruit And Train
wheelRecruitTrain.description: Wheel Recruit / Train adds troops and trains artillery by armament level.

steps.overview: Wheel Recruit / Train is not only about placing new blocks. It also consumes the armament levels you have already developed.
steps.chooseMove: Click the wheel's "Move 1 for free" option to advance the public wheel from Military Farm into Recruit / Train.
steps.result: Wheel Recruit / Train has resolved. The two new level-2 regular troops on the map are the recruitment result; if Artillery Technology has already advanced, existing artillery is trained upward at the same time.
steps.finish: This shows the wheel is not just rotating through labels. It is tying armaments, troop growth, and the live front together in one real result.

armamentUpgrade.title: Armament Upgrade
armamentUpgrade.description: Armament upgrade spends hand cards and updates the armament level on the live board.

steps.overview: Armaments do not grow for free. You still spend hand cards to push them higher.
steps.chooseAction: Click "Artillery Technology" in your hand to enter Armament Upgrade. You still discard 1 more hand card before that armament rises by 1 level.
steps.payCards: Pick 2 cards from the hand at the bottom, then confirm the action.
steps.result: The upgrade is now live: Ming Artillery Technology has gone from level 1 to level 2, and the armament summary in the player strip updates with it.
steps.finish: This hand action does not change the map directly. It improves the armament level that later battles will use.

eventAction.title: Khan's Edict
eventAction.description: Khan's Edict is the Mongol faction action. It resolves through payment, effect choice, and result, with the discard and map change landing together.

steps.overview: Mongol faction actions are also paid with hand cards. Khan's Edict turns this action into recruit/training or diplomacy/hire.
steps.chooseAction: Click the Khan's Edict faction action on the right. After it starts, discard 1 hand card to enter the effect choice.
steps.payCards: Pick 1 card from the hand at the bottom, then confirm the action.
steps.chooseEffect: Click Shanhaiguan on the map first to confirm where Khan's Edict will add troops, then choose Recruit / Train to resolve the gain.
steps.result: After Khan's Edict resolves, look at Shanhaiguan on the map: Mongol troops increase from 2 to 4.
steps.finish: That is the faction-action rhythm: spend a card to fire it, then let the action effect change the live position immediately.

diplomacy.title: Diplomacy And Hire
diplomacy.description: Enter a real wheel diplomacy step and see control markers and hired troops resolve together.

steps.overview: Diplomacy decides regional relationships, not just marker sides; hiring decides where new troops can appear.
steps.wheelEntry: Push the wheel into Diplomacy and Hire. This branch resolves control relationships and room for troops, not battle.
steps.chooseTarget: Diplomacy targets map regions. Click a region adjacent to your controlled areas; you cannot target homeland regions without control markers, Korea regions, or areas with regular troops stationed there.
steps.friendlyMark: Click Ningyuan on the map to place a friendly marker. A reverse-side marker means your troops may pass through and station there, but it is not yet a controlled region.
steps.tributeMark: Flip the friendly marker you just placed into a vassal marker. Only a face-up marker counts as your controlled region; neutral regions taken by battle also become this state directly.
steps.removeMark: Click Dongjiang on the map and remove the existing rival control marker. Diplomacy not only places your own markers; it can also push back markers already placed by someone else.
steps.finish: After diplomacy and hiring finish, return to the map: the Ningyuan marker changed, and hired troops landed in a controlled region.

yearAndCharacters.title: Midyear, New Year, And Chronology
yearAndCharacters.description: Midyear taxes, character checks, New Year maintenance, attrition, chronology scoring, and turn-order refresh form the yearly resolution.

steps.overview: This chapter first advances the public wheel into Midyear, then into New Year, so taxes, character checks, fortification maintenance, and attrition resolve in sequence.
steps.advanceMidyear: Click the wheel's "one opponent draws 2, move 2" option to advance the action marker into Midyear.
steps.midyearTax: After Midyear taxes resolve, look at the player strip: Xuanfu's population surplus has become resources; besieged controlled regions do not collect that tax.
steps.midyearCharacters: After the character checks resolve, look at the player strip: character states and defeat markers have updated.
steps.advanceNewYear: After Midyear resolves, click the wheel's "Move 1 for free" option to advance the action marker into New Year.
steps.newYearTribute: New Year Korean tribute: whoever controls Korean regions draws the matching number of Korea cards shown on the map.
steps.newYearMaintenance: Then click "Auto pay" to handle fortification maintenance. If the Great Wall, Shanhaiguan, Ningyuan, or Jinzhou cannot be maintained, they fall into ruin and their border and city effects fail with them.
steps.newYearAttrition: After maintenance, look at the player strip and map: unsupported troops have entered attrition, and the remaining force is what you can actually use next year.
steps.chronologyScore: Chronology cards are not just year markers. The player with the highest score must pay half their hand to claim that year's prestige, or pass the chance to the next player.
steps.turnOrderRefresh: Once chronology resolves, both turn order and new characters refresh, and next year's tempo changes with them.
steps.finish: When a year closes, read three formal areas: the player strip for resources and characters, the map for troops, and the turn banner for next year's current actor.

koreaSpecial.title: Korea And Special Map Rules
koreaSpecial.description: Korea, Hanseong, sea routes, and Shanhaiguan are map-specific rules that directly change play.

steps.overview: This chapter checks Korea, Hanseong, waterways, and Shanhaiguan on the map, then connects them to Korean attrition through New Year maintenance.
steps.koreaRegion: Start with Korea. Tribute icons on each region decide how many Korea cards are drawn at New Year, and control decides who receives them.
steps.hanseongVp: Then check Hanseong prestige on the player bar. Once Ming loses its initial control, whoever controls Hanseong effectively gains 1 prestige.
steps.waterLimit: Sea routes between anchor regions can move at most 2 troops at a time, and cavalry cannot use sea routes to evade battle.
steps.newYearMaintenance: Now click "Auto pay" to handle New Year maintenance. After maintenance resolves, troops in Korea also enter attrition resolution.
steps.koreaAttrition: Korean regions provide no population support. After New Year resolves, read the Korea rail and map troops together to see which units took attrition.
steps.shanhaiguan: Look at Shanhaiguan on the map: it is both a city and a special border between Jizhen and Liaoxi; intact keeps the border narrow, while ruin widens it.
steps.finish: These special cases produce real turn results: Korea decides who draws tribute at New Year, waterways decide how troops move, Shanhaiguan changes borders and city defense, and Hanseong changes prestige. They are not merely optional notes.
